peopleAlsoAsk: What is the most popular alcoholic drink in Thailand?
What alcohol to avoid in Thailand?
Why can't you buy alcohol between 2pm and 5pm in Thailand?

items.markdown:
Popular Thai alcoholic drinks include Singha beer, Sang Som rum, and local rice spirits like [Lao Khao](https://www.tasteatlas.com/lao-khao) . These beverages range from crisp, refreshing lagers meant for hot weather to potent sugarcane and rice-based liquors deeply rooted in local traditions.[](https://www.raanthai.co.uk/collections/thai-alcoholic-drinks) [[1]](https://www.raanthai.co.uk/collections/thai-alcoholic-drinks)[[2]](https://www.tasteatlas.com/best-rated-alcoholic-beverages-in-thailand)[[3]](https://www.thailanna.co.uk/about-thai-food/drinks-for-thai-food/)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RNk3OCOzs8I&t=65)[[5]](https://www.traveltalktours.com/thai-food/)

Beers

- **Singha:** Thailand's oldest and most famous premium pale lager (5% ABV), known for its rich, malty flavor.
- **Chang:** A budget-friendly, crisp lager (typically 5% ABV) that is very popular across the country and pairs well with spicy food.
- **Leo:** A smooth, easy-drinking standard lager (5% ABV) widely found in local bars and restaurants.[](https://www.raanthai.co.uk/collections/thai-alcoholic-drinks) [[1]](https://www.everydaybangkokhostel.com/thai-beer/)[[2]](https://pacsafe.co.uk/blogs/pacsafe-blog/7-best-beers-in-thailand)[[3]](https://www.a2zdrinks.com/singha-premium-thai-lager-beer-bottle-24-x-330-ml-5-abv.html)

Spirits and Whiskeys

- **Sang Som:** A heavily popular Thai rum (40% ABV) distilled from molasses, featuring a sweet, vanilla-and-caramel profile often mixed with soda or cola.[](https://www.raanthai.co.uk/collections/thai-alcoholic-drinks) 
- **Mekhong:** Launched in 1941 as Thailand's first branded spirit, it is a golden liquor (35% ABV) distilled from molasses and rice, then infused with local herbs and spices.[](https://www.tasteatlas.com/best-rated-alcoholic-beverages-in-thailand) 
- **Lao Khao:** A clear, potent white rice spirit traditionally moonshined in villages, though commercial versions are widely sold and used as a base for herbal infusions.[](https://www.tasteatlas.com/best-rated-alcoholic-beverages-in-thailand) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RNk3OCOzs8I&t=65)
- **Yaa Dong:** A traditional Thai herbal spirit made by steeping Lao Khao with local roots, barks, and spices, traditionally taken in small shots for medicinal or energizing properties.[](https://factsanddetails.com/southeast-asia/Thailand/sub5_8d/entry-3238.html) [[1]](https://factsanddetails.com/southeast-asia/Thailand/sub5_8d/entry-3238.html)[[2]](https://www.masterofmalt.com/country/thai-spirit/)[[3]](https://thaisq.com/all-you-ever-wanted-to-know-about-thai-whiskey/)[[4]](https://www.atlasobscura.com/itineraries/best-restaurants-bars-bangkok)[[5]](https://explorepartsunknown.com/thailand/bottoms-up-the-evolution-of-thai-spirits/)

Rice Wine and Craft Options

- **Sato:** A cloudy, sweet traditional rice wine from Northeast Thailand (Isan) made by fermenting glutinous rice with a starter yeast called *lukpaeng*.[](https://www.tasteatlas.com/best-rated-alcoholic-beverages-in-thailand) 
- **Chalong Bay & Saneha:** Modern craft spirits from Phuket, including premium white sugarcane rum and botanical craft gins infused with local Thai ingredients like lemongrass and ginger.[](https://www.tasteatlas.com/best-rated-alcoholic-beverages-in-thailand) [[1]](https://www.rhumattitude.com/en/cave/saneha-40/)

expanded_element.description:
Mekhong – The Spirit of Thailand
 It's famously used in the Thai Sabai cocktail, a refreshing concoction of Mekhong, lime juice, and Thai basil. Mekhong's rich history as the first branded Thai spirit adds a sense of pride and tradition, often making it the drink of choice during festivals and national celebrations.

expanded_element.description:
Methanol poisoning
 There have been deaths and cases of serious illness caused by alcoholic drinks containing methanol in Thailand. Even small amounts of methanol can kill. It is not possible to identify methanol in alcoholic drinks by taste or smell.
